note: Single source of truth for this brain's data contract. Templates, JSON Schemas, the catalog, the portable bundle schema, the skill stubs, the directory indexes, the derived indexes and (in cut 2) the SQLite DDL are all GENERATED from this file. Never edit a generated artifact; edit this and run `brain generate`. READING ORDER -- the top-level keys are ordered as a narrative, separated by blank lines, rather than nested into groups: (1) what this contract is -- note, versions, provenance, governance, and the policies it is written under; (2) the vocabulary the schema is written in -- the validity model, data types, actors, and the classification ladder, each defined before it is used; (3) the schema itself -- common_fields and types, which are 59% of the file; (4) the files it produces -- reserved, exempt, derived, the portable bundle schema and the SQLite projection. Grouping these into nested objects was considered and rejected: the groups are wildly uneven, the boundaries are genuinely ambiguous (classification is both vocabulary and policy), and nesting would lengthen every access path and every provenance entry for no functional gain.

provenance.note: What comes from the OKF specification and what is ours. This block exists because the file used to be named okf.json, which implied the whole thing was the standard -- it is not, and the confusion had a cost: it was unclear what to update when a new OKF version ships. The answer is now exact: the items under `from_okf`, and nothing else.
provenance.ours: Everything not listed above. OKF leaves `type` producer-defined and takes no position on a field-level type system, data classification, stewardship, derived files, severity policy or generation -- which is most of this file by volume. Our additions extend the standard; they never contradict it, and the validator keeps the two levels apart so a bundle stays OKF-conformant even when it fails our profile.
provenance.completeness_rule: Every entry of `common_fields` must appear in exactly one of the three lists. A new common field therefore forces a conscious answer to 'is this the standard's or ours?', which is the question the old filename made impossible to answer. Enforced by kernel/tests/test_roundtrip.py.

governance.note: Makes this contract a governed artifact rather than a file someone edits. Governance that lives only in prose is what v1 had, and it enforced nothing.
governance.steward: El dueño del cerebro, declarado en cerebro/PERFIL.md. Del contrato base responde quien mantiene el starter.
governance.steward_note: Spanish because `governance_report` renders it to a person, per language_policy -- same rule as `review_cadence`. It was a `<TODO: /x-setup>` placeholder, which meant the posture report of a governed artifact answered 'who is responsible' with a TODO. It names a ROLE and not a person on purpose: this file ships in a public starter, and the individual varies per install.
governance.change_process: A contract change is a PR to the starter, never a local edit. Bump `profile_version` when tightening a constraint. No type enters without a competency question that needs it.
governance.review_cadence: Una vez por periodo de planificación, junto con /x-cierre-periodo.
governance.enforcement: `brain.py validate` on pre-commit (only what changes) and in CI (the whole bundle). A control nobody runs is not a control.

language_policy.note: The rule, stated as a test rather than a preference: ANY string this contract renders into an artifact a person reads is content and is Spanish; everything else is configuration and is English. In practice that means `note` is always English -- it is commentary for whoever maintains the contract, and nothing renders it -- while `placeholder`, `guide`, `heading`, the `bundle_schema` strings, the `derived_files` strings and the classification `description`/`handling` are always Spanish. Field KEYS stay as production writes them. Enum VALUES split by scope: per-type enums are Spanish because they live in 10.000 documents and renaming them is a corpus migration; the two common-field enums (`status`, `classification`) are English because they travel in every document next to each other and `status` comes from OKF.
language_policy.history: Two leaks were found by applying this rule after the fact. The classification `description`/`handling` had been translated to English and were rendering inside the bundle's own ESQUEMA.md. And `placeholder` did not exist: the generator fell back to `note`, so `Sistema.dueño` emitted a full English paragraph about migration costs and check numbers into the user's document. Separating the two roles is what fixed it -- one string cannot serve both an engineer and a reader.

location_rules.note: Locations are ROUTING data, not documentation. `brain place` answers 'where does this document go', so /x-procesar-inbox no longer decides destinations from prose spread across three skill modules, and V19 validates against the same declaration. A pattern may be a plain string or an object with `when` (same shape as derived_files.where) and `role`.
location_rules.placeholders: Every `{name}` in a path must be a field the type declares. Enforced by kernel/tests/test_roundtrip.py -- making locations routable is what exposed that Insumo, Playbook and Iniciativa itself referenced `{proyecto}` without declaring it.
location_rules.ambiguity: If exactly one pattern applies, `brain place` answers. If several do, it returns the candidates and the agent chooses. The tool removes the prose, never the judgement.

roles.archive: dónde queda tras /x-cierre-periodo; válido para validar, nunca para enrutar

citation_rules.note: The citation lock, structural half. OKF is explicit that consumers MUST tolerate broken links, and V10 honours that: a broken link in the BODY is INFO, because it marks knowledge not yet written. A broken link under the citations heading is a different act. A citation asserts that a source exists and supports a claim, so a citation that resolves to nothing is a FABRICATED citation -- and a fabricated citation is worse than an unsourced claim, because the unsourced claim is read with suspicion and the false citation is read with trust (ADV-13). Not a heritage case to tolerate while the corpus migrates: a defect at any scale. The `/raw/` prefix is exempt, as everywhere: it points outside the bundle on purpose, and a brain shared without its sources has those links broken by design -- `brain verify-raw` is what checks those. The other half of the lock -- that a document may only cite what its author actually opened -- the validator cannot see, because it has no session. That half lives in the skill modules, and is stated below so the rule is written once.
citation_rules.heading: Citations
agent_rules_es: La sección de fuentes se arma desde la lista de documentos que ABRISTE en esta sesión, no desde lo que recuerdes haber leído.
Solo se cita lo que se abrió. Si no puedes armar la lista, no respondas afirmando: dilo, y abre una `Pregunta`.
Una cita apunta a un documento que existe. Si el documento que querías citar no está escrito todavía, eso es un hueco declarado, no una cita.
El puntero `/raw/...` es la excepción: apunta fuera del bundle a propósito, y se comprueba con `./brain verify-raw`.

frontmatter_rules.note: Rules an agent must follow when WRITING frontmatter. They exist because our parser is deliberately lenient and the viewer the user opens is not: a value our validator accepted made Obsidian and VS Code fail with 'mapping values are not allowed here', and users reported it. Enforced by V18, so this is a check and not a suggestion.
agent_rules_es: Nunca escribas `: ` (dos puntos y espacio) dentro de un valor sin entrecomillar. Es el indicador de clave y valor en YAML, y rompe el visor. Usa una coma, un guion o un punto y coma — o entrecomilla el valor completo.

Nunca escribas ` #` (espacio y almohadilla) dentro de un valor: YAML lo lee como comentario y **borra en silencio todo lo que sigue**. Ni siquiera `--fix` puede recuperarlo, porque no hay forma de saber si querías un comentario.
No empieces un valor por `- ? : , [ ] { } # & * ! | > ' " % @` — todos son indicadores de YAML.
Para un campo de texto, si el valor es `true`, `no`, `on`, `null` o parece un número, entrecomíllalo: YAML lo convertiría de tipo.
Ante la duda, entrecomilla con comillas dobles y escapa las que haya dentro. Entrecomillar de más nunca rompe nada.
La prosa larga va en el cuerpo del documento, no en el frontmatter. El frontmatter es para metadatos cortos y consultables.
frontmatter_rules.auto_fix: `brain.py validate --fix` entrecomilla los valores cuyo significado no cambia al hacerlo, y lo verifica reparseando cada línea antes de escribirla. Los que sí cambiarían de significado se reportan para que los resuelva una persona.

severity_policy.note: Migration ladder. Constraints that v1's templates already guaranteed ship as `error`. Constraints introduced by OKF v0.2 ship as `warning` in profile_version 1, so a real brain does not light up on day one. Tightening a constraint means flipping it to `error` and bumping profile_version.

validity_model.note: Which field answers «is this still true?». It is written here because the answer used to be spread across SIX mechanisms that nobody had listed side by side -- and the contract itself admitted one of them was redundant (`Lineamiento.vigencia`: «does the same job as `estado` elsewhere»). Six overlapping answers do not make a system stricter; they make it impossible to say which one is right when they disagree. T9 (2026-09-14) assigned one axis to each.
validity_model.principle: ONE FACT, ONE PLACE. The interval is the only source of «did it rule?»; every other field answers a different question.

world_time.answers: Between which dates was it true IN THE WORLD? Not when it was written: a decision taken in July can rule from May.

lifecycle.answers: Where is the SUBJECT in its own cycle -- proposed, accepted, under review? Never whether it still rules.

editorial.answers: Is the DOCUMENT finished or withdrawn? OKF's, untouched: a stable document can describe a rule that expired.

review.answers: When should someone look at this again? OKF's, untouched. It asks for a review, it does not claim anything expired.

derived_states.note: The three states that used to be enum values are now QUERIES. That is the point: an enum value can contradict the dates beside it; a query cannot.
derived_states.reemplazada: valido_hasta IS NOT NULL AND reemplazada_por IS NOT NULL
derived_states.caducada: valido_hasta IS NOT NULL AND reemplazada_por IS NULL

validity_model.view_note: One view over every type that carries an interval, so CQ-48 and CQ-51 are answered across both instead of once per type. The derived state is a CASE built from `derived_states` above -- the three sentences that used to be enum values are generated from the contract, not retyped in SQL, so they cannot drift apart from what the contract says they mean.
validity_model.rejected: A `rechazada` value for the half of `obsoleta` the interval cannot express -- a proposal studied and turned down. No competency question asks for it, and the contract's cutting rule is explicit: a value no question needs does not enter. Recorded here so the next person does not re-derive the idea and assume it was overlooked.

datetime.note: ISO 8601 with an explicit UTC offset, e.g. 2026-08-28T14:00:00Z

list.note: inline [a, b] or block; element type in `of`

link.note: bundle-relative path starting with /, or the reserved /raw/ pointer

typed-ref.note: link whose target must carry the type named in `to`

type-key.hint: el slug del proyecto; `transversal` si no pertenece a ninguno
type-key.note: reference by KEY VALUE rather than by path: the value must match the `key` field of some document of type `to`. Exists because `proyecto: 2026-q3-erp` is written that way in every document in production -- turning it into a link would be a corpus migration. `sentinels` lists values that are valid without resolving.

person-ref.note: accountability pointer. A bundle link to a Persona resolves and is checked; free text is tolerated and reported by V17 as unresolved stewardship. Migration-friendly by design: ownership becomes queryable progressively instead of behind a wall of errors.

actor.note: matches one of the patterns in `actors`

map.note: single-level inline mapping; member types in `fields`

actors.note: Per OKF v0.2 section 7. Trust classification keys off the `human:` prefix, so it must be used for hand-authored or human-confirmed content. There is no `agent:` prefix -- agents use producer/version.

user_contract.note: What cerebro/schema.json may declare. Everything here is dispatched by `mode`, so the next user-settable knob is a contract edit and not a code change. An undeclared key is an ERROR rather than silence: a typo in a config file that quietly does nothing is the failure this whole block exists to remove.

types.note: User types are ADDED. Base types can be neither overridden nor removed.

period_format.note: The NAME of one shape -- quarterly, monthly or sprint -- never a regex. Writing the pattern is the kernel's job.

period_formats.note: The planning cycle's period format. It lived as prose in cerebro/PERFIL.md and drifted unchecked: `2026-Q3`, `2026-q3`, `Q3-2026`, `tercer trimestre` and `T3` all validated, because `periodo` is a text field and `text` has no branch in check_value. The user picks ONE shape BY NAME in cerebro/schema.json; the regex is written here, by whoever knows how to write one. Every shape sorts lexicographically, because these values are also the folder names under 04-archivo/ -- and folders sort.
period_formats.undeclared: A value is accepted if it matches ANY shape. That catches `tercer trimestre` without demanding configuration and without assuming a cycle the user never chose. /x-setup always declares one, so this only covers v1 brains mid-migration.

monthly.description: Mensual. Mes a dos dígitos, con cero a la izquierda.

sprint.description: Sprints numerados dentro del año, a dos dígitos con cero a la izquierda.

classification.note: Proposed taxonomy: the organization had none defined. Four levels ordered from least to most restrictive. The ORDER is load-bearing -- V16 compares against each type's floor. If the organization adopts its own taxonomy, replace it here and every generated artifact follows.
classification.min_note: Per-type floor. `min_classification` is declared only where it exceeds `default_min`, so the exception is the thing you read. A document BELOW its floor is an ERROR, never a warning: it is the one classification control that does not relax during migration.
classification.value_language_note: These enum VALUES are English, unlike every other enum in this contract. The reason the others stayed Spanish was migration cost -- they live in the frontmatter of every document in production. This field is new in v2, so no document carries it and the cost is zero. It also sits next to `status` (draft|stable|deprecated, from OKF) in every single document, and two adjacent lifecycle enums in two languages is a wart. The resulting line is principled rather than arbitrary: COMMON fields follow OKF and are English; PER-TYPE fields follow production and are Spanish.

levels.description: Puede salir de la organización sin daño.
Uso interno; sin daño material si circula dentro de la organización.
levels.handling: No compartir fuera. Es el piso por defecto: la ausencia de clasificación nunca significa público.

levels.description: Limitado a quien lo necesita. Incluye dato personal, información de clientes y detalle operativo sensible.
levels.handling: No compartir fuera del equipo con necesidad de conocer. Revisar antes de exportar un cerebro que los contenga.

levels.description: Material regulatorio, legal o de seguridad. Su divulgación tiene consecuencias formales.
levels.handling: Requiere autorización explícita del dueño del dato. Revisar antes de cualquier compartición o respaldo fuera del perímetro.

type.note: The only field OKF always requires. A concept carrying just `type` is fully conformant.

description.placeholder: qué es y por qué importa, en una oración
description.note: one sentence: what it is and why it matters

tags.hint: etiquetas cortas para agrupar; lista vacía es válida

classification.note: Sensitivity level. The allowed values are RESOLVED from the taxonomy at load time rather than repeated here -- writing the list twice in one file is exactly the drift this contract exists to prevent, and it had been written twice. Required, but only a warning in profile 1 because the production corpus does not carry it yet. Each type declares a `min_classification`; going below it is an error, not a warning. Replaces v1's prose rule (`no sensitive data`), which enforced nothing because it lived inside a template guide string.

generated.hint: quién produjo el documento y cuándo cambió su contenido por última vez
generated.note: OKF v0.2. `at` is the time of the last meaningful content change. Replaces v1's `timestamp`.

verified.hint: sin una entrada de un actor `human:`, el documento es una propuesta, no conocimiento
verified.note: OKF v0.2. A bare mapping MUST be treated as a one-element list. A document with no verified entry from a `human:` actor is a proposal, not knowledge -- this is the human-review rule expressed in the schema instead of in a prompt.

sources.hint: de dónde salió cada afirmación; `resource` es obligatorio en cada entrada

resource.note: absolute URL, bundle-relative path, or /raw/ pointer

id.note: stable key for per-claim attribution via footnotes

status.note: OKF v0.2 lifecycle. Absent means stable.

stale_after.hint: fecha a partir de la cual el dato debe revisarse antes de usarse
stale_after.note: OKF v0.2. A concept is stale once now >= stale_after. Turns obsolescence from a judgement call into a date comparison.

resumen.placeholder: panorama en ~600 caracteres: qué dice este documento y qué decide quien lo lee
resumen.hint: el nivel intermedio de lectura: lo que permite DESCARTAR un documento sin abrirlo
resumen.note: L1 of the read budget (`read_budget`). Deliberately AUTHORED, not mechanically extracted from headings: a table of contents does not let a reader discard a document and an overview does. This is the field that attacks the 95% -- survey.py measured 3.285 tokens to find candidates and 61.731 to open them, so orientation is where the cost is. Written by the agent at ingest under human review; the deterministic layer only ever writes a MECHANICAL one, for generated indexes, where the summary genuinely is mechanical. Its staleness check (V23, against `resumen_hash`) arrives with T2: until then the field exists and nothing guards it drifting from the body.

resumen_hash.placeholder: sha256 del cuerpo, que imprime `./brain hash ARCHIVO --body` (o lo escribe `--write`)
resumen_hash.note: SHA-256 of the BODY at the moment the `resumen` was written, so V23 can say the summary went stale. Hashes the body and never the frontmatter, because the value lives in the frontmatter and hashing itself would change what it hashes -- that is exactly why `path`/`hash` of the projection are NOT common fields, and why this one legitimately is. Required but relaxed while the corpus migrates: 301 documents predate it. NEVER filled in by `validate --fix`: recomputing it would silence V23 without anyone having checked that the summary still describes the body, which is falsifying the guarantee rather than repairing it. It is written by whoever writes the summary, in the same breath.

procedencia.hint: cómo entró la afirmación: leída de un insumo, dicha en una conversación, inferida por un agente, escrita por una persona, o derivada mecánicamente
procedencia.note: How the assertion ENTERED, which `actors` does not answer: it says WHO wrote the document. An agent transcribing a PDF and an agent inferring from a discussion are the same actor with different reliability, and today the system stores them identically -- CQ-52. Named `procedencia` and not `origen` because that key is already taken twice with two different data types (`Iniciativa.origen` is an enum, `Insumo.origen` a /raw/ link) and `derived_files.GOALS.md` groups by it. `derivado` is the fifth value and was not in the original four: generated indexes assert nothing of their own, and calling them `inferido` would poison the very distinction this field exists to draw -- inference is fallible, a derived index is deterministic.

source_rule.note: Saying `fuente` is claiming the statement was READ somewhere, so the document has to say where -- otherwise the most trustworthy value is also the cheapest to write, which is backwards. V25 enforces it. `Insumo.origen` counts as much as `sources`: the converter writes the /raw/ pointer there, and demanding the same path twice in two fields would only create two places to disagree. A warning while the corpus migrates -- the field was born on 2026-09-11 and the 301 documents predate it -- and it tightens to error after the step-9 migration, exactly as `classification` does.

timestamp.note: v1 field, not part of OKF. `brain validate --fix` moves it to generated.at and leaves generated.by as a declared gap when git history cannot resolve it.

Iniciativa.description: The CONTEXT.md of each project or objective with an identity of its own
Iniciativa.key_unique_note: Two Iniciativa documents cannot share a slug. It is the identity every other type points at with `proyecto`, so a duplicate makes every reference ambiguous -- and V20 would not see it, because resolving finds one and finding one is enough. Enforced in three places, each doing what only it can: V27 catches it in an existing brain, the `UNIQUE` of the projection stops it reaching the database, and /x-nueva-iniciativa checks before creating, which is the only one that prevents it instead of reporting it.

proyecto.note: The project slug, and the identity every other type points at with `proyecto`. It existed only as a folder name until now, so nothing could resolve a reference to it and cut 2 would have had to derive the join key from the file path.

periodo.note: shape named by `period_format` in cerebro/schema.json; the regex lives in `period_formats` and V21 enforces it. Presence stays an error (v1 templates guaranteed it); the FORMAT enters as a warning, per severity_policy

sections.heading: Qué es
sections.guide: Un párrafo: qué se construye/modifica, para quién, por qué ahora.

sections.heading: Qué significa "entregado"
sections.guide: La definición de éxito. Los agentes la usan como directiva: si una sesión deriva sin avanzar hacia esto, señalarlo.

sections.heading: Personas clave
sections.guide: enlace a la ficha + su rol en esta iniciativa

sections.heading: Estado actual
sections.guide: Última actualización, estado corto, qué pasó, qué sigue, qué bloquea.

Plan.description: The PLAN.md of a project: the tasks that lead to "delivered", grouped by phase
Plan.note: Introduced by v1 kernel 1.4.0. Its task rows live INSIDE the document as a markdown table, which is the first structured data this system has below document level. That is why cerebro/PENDIENTES.md cannot be generated yet -- see its entry in derived_files.

proyecto.note: No `transversal` sentinel, unlike every other type keyed on a project: a PLAN.md lives inside a project folder by definition, so a plan with no project cannot exist. Declaring a value valid with nowhere to put it is the defect this removal closes.

fuente-de-verdad.hint: `externa` si las tareas ya viven en Jira, Asana o un Excel del área; entonces este plan es un espejo y ningún skill afirma progreso global

tracker-externo.placeholder: URL o nombre del tracker real

ultima-revision.placeholder: AAAA-MM-DD de la última vez que se revisó contra la realidad

conditions.note: A plan declared a mirror with no pointer to what it mirrors is worse than no plan: it looks authoritative and is not.

sections.heading: Entregado
sections.guide: Copia literal de la definición de «entregado» del CONTEXT.md. Toda tarea rastrea hasta acá: si no aporta a eso, sobra.

sections.heading: Fases
sections.guide: una subsección por fase, con su hito y su tabla de tareas: # · Tarea · Responsable · Estado · Límite · Origen

sections.heading: Fuera de alcance
sections.guide: lo que se decidió NO hacer, con una línea de por qué, para que no vuelva a discutirse

sections.heading: Citations
sections.guide: el insumo, la reunión o la decisión de donde salieron las tareas

Insumo.description: A received document converted to markdown, pointing at its original in /raw/
Insumo.governance_note: External material whose content the system does not control. The raised floor forces a conscious declassification instead of assuming what arrived is harmless.
Insumo.note: Not hand-written: `to-markdown.py` emits it. Known v1 drift this contract now catches: .htm and .yml produced `formato: htm` / `formato: yml`, outside the enum.

origen.note: /raw/ pointer to the immutable original. Distinct meaning from Iniciativa.origen -- same key, different type, which is why fields are declared per type.

sections.heading: Avisos de conversión
sections.guide: Los que emitió el script. Si no hay ninguno, se quita la sección. Nunca se borra un aviso sin resolverlo.

sections.heading: Contenido
sections.guide: El markdown que produjo la conversión. No se edita para mejorarlo.

sections.heading: Citations
sections.guide: [1] Original: enlace a /raw/

sections.heading: Resumen
sections.guide: 3-5 líneas: de qué fue la reunión y qué salió de ella.

sections.heading: Decisiones tomadas
sections.guide: decisión — quién la tomó / contexto. Si es importante, registrarla con /x-decision y enlazarla.

sections.heading: Preguntas abiertas surgidas
sections.guide: cada una crea su documento Pregunta y se enlaza

sections.heading: Notas
sections.guide: Detalle relevante que no encaja arriba. Autocontenido: que se entienda sin leer la transcripción.

sections.heading: Citations
sections.guide: [1] Original: enlace a /raw/

Decision.description: Record of a decision with its context, alternatives and consequences

estado.note: The SUBJECT's lifecycle, and only that. `reemplazada` and `obsoleta` were removed in T9: whether something still rules is the interval's job, and having both meant two fields answering one question and eventually disagreeing. `rechazada` was considered for the half of `obsoleta` the interval cannot express -- a proposal studied and turned down -- and left out because no competency question asks for it. The cutting rule is explicit: a value no question needs does not enter.

valido_desde.note: When it STARTED to hold in the world, which is not when it was written: a decision taken in July can rule from May. Empty means it held from its `fecha`.

valido_hasta.note: When it STOPPED holding. Empty means it still holds -- that is the whole definition of `vigente`, and why it is not an enum value. With `reemplazada_por` it was superseded; without it, it simply expired, which is CQ-51.

reemplazada_por.note: GENEALOGY: what replaced it. Not whether it still rules -- that is `valido_hasta`. The two together are what separates «superseded» from «expired», which no single field could say. (It used to be described here as the hook for cut 3's bi-temporal fact model; T9 replaced that plan with the declared interval, and this note is rewritten rather than left describing a design that is no longer the live one.)

sections.heading: Contexto
sections.guide: Qué problema o fuerza motiva la decisión. Enlazar documentos, reuniones y lineamientos aplicables.

sections.heading: Opciones consideradas
sections.guide: una subsección por opción, con pros y contras

sections.heading: Decisión
sections.guide: Qué se decidió y por qué. Verificar contra decisiones previas y lineamientos: si contradice alguno, decirlo explícitamente.

sections.heading: Consecuencias
sections.guide: positivas, negativas, compromisos asumidos, trabajo que habilita o bloquea

sections.heading: Citations
sections.guide: reunión, lineamiento o documento que respalda la decisión

Pregunta.description: An open question with a status and an owner

responsable.hint: a quién se le pregunta; vacío es un hueco declarado, nunca un supuesto
responsable.note: who to ask. Empty is a declared gap, never a guess.

respondida_por.note: new in v2: what answered it

sections.heading: Contexto
sections.guide: De dónde salió la duda. Enlazar la reunión o documento fuente.

sections.heading: Avances
sections.guide: fecha — lo averiguado hasta ahora, aunque sea parcial

sections.heading: Respuesta
sections.guide: Pendiente hasta responderse. Al responderse: respuesta completa + fuente + fecha. Evaluar si debe promoverse a Sistema o Lineamiento.

Persona.description: Profile of a person in the organization
Persona.governance_note: Holds personal data: name, role, reporting line. The floor is enforced by code, not by a prose rule. This is also the first type to review before any sharing or export of the brain.

reporta-a.hint: vacío es un hueco declarado con su Pregunta; nunca se infiere de un correo ni de un organigrama parcial
reporta-a.note: empty is a declared gap in the org chart and must have its own Pregunta. Never inferred from an email header or a partial chart.

sections.heading: Qué sabe / qué maneja
sections.guide: dominios, sistemas o temas en los que es la referencia

sections.heading: Cómo trabaja
sections.guide: preferencias, estilo, canales, cosas a tener en cuenta

sections.heading: Historial relevante
sections.guide: fecha — decisión, dato o interacción importante

Sistema.description: Profile of a system, tool, product or process of the organization

dueño.placeholder: enlace a la ficha de quien responde, o su nombre
dueño.note: owner of the system. The key carries an n-tilde and is kept as-is: renaming it would be a migration of every brain in production. As a person-ref, a free-text name is tolerated and reported by V17 until it resolves to a ficha.

sections.heading: Qué hace
sections.guide: Descripción funcional. Sin datos sensibles ni de seguridad.

sections.heading: Cómo se relaciona

fuente.placeholder: quién lo definió — enlace a ficha, comité o área
fuente.note: who defined it. Accepts a committee or an area as free text; V17 reports it until it points at a ficha.

estado.note: Renamed from `vigencia` in T9 -- it did the same job as `estado` elsewhere under another name, and the compatibility that justified keeping it was retired. `derogado` left the enum: a repealed guideline is one with a `valido_hasta` in the past, which also says WHEN it stopped applying, something the enum never could. And `vigente` was renamed to `aprobado` on 2026-09-14, when ADV-01 was written as a query and turned out to describe a defect in THIS FILE: after T9 the field no longer decides whether something rules, but the value was still called `vigente` -- so an agent reading `estado: vigente` on an expired guideline would present it as in force, which is exactly what ADV-01 forbids. A value whose NAME contradicts the model is a trap, and renaming it costs one enum in a type with 8 documents. `aprobado` also lines the type up with `Decision.estado`.

fecha.note: When it was written down. The interval says when it RULED.

valido_desde.note: When it STARTED to hold in the world, which is not when it was written: a decision taken in July can rule from May. Empty means it held from its `fecha`.

valido_hasta.note: When it STOPPED holding. Empty means it still holds -- that is the whole definition of `vigente`, and why it is not an enum value. With `reemplazada_por` it was superseded; without it, it simply expired, which is CQ-51.

reemplazada_por.note: Same genealogy as in `Decision`. A guideline is superseded as often as a decision, and until T9 there was nowhere to say so.

Glosario.description: A term, acronym or piece of internal jargon
Glosario.note: STRUCTURAL, decided 2026-08-31. No competency question needs it as a subject and it declares no required fields -- its content is prose by nature, so nothing about it is queryable. The cutting rule would drop it; it stays for the reason `Insumo` and `Indice` stay: it serves by being READ, not queried. Cutting it would also solve nothing -- OKF requires a `type` on every knowledge file, production holds 8 of these, and no other type houses the definition of a term. Not modelled in the cut-2 projection beyond its identity.

Playbook.description: A reusable step-by-step process, meant to be followed again
Playbook.note: Split from `Analisis` on 2026-08-31. It was defined as a reusable process OR an archived analysis -- the OR was the defect, and the competency questions forced the answer the cutting rule promised: CQ-44 asks for processes to reuse (decision: reutilizar en vez de improvisar) while CQ-34 asks for precedent not to repeat. Different `decision`, `frequency` and `answer_shape`, so two types. The cut: a Playbook is FOLLOWED, an Analisis is CONSULTED -- if a document does not say `next time, do this`, it is not a Playbook. MIGRATION: production holds 23 documents of this type needing triage by hand; /x-nueva-iniciativa creates analisis-inicial.md as a Playbook, and those are Analisis. STILL UNRESOLVED: v1 cerebro/GOALS.md carries this type and is neither -- it is period objectives, and no competency question asks for it.

Analisis.note: The half of the old `Playbook` that is consulted rather than followed, split out on 2026-08-31. Kept because CQ-34 -- what is on record about this from earlier periods -- is answered by archived analyses as much as by decisions and initiatives, and its decision is `no repetir un intento ya hecho`. Spanish and unaccented, like `Reunion` and `Decision`. Named deliberately away from `Informe`, `Entregable` and `Recurso`: the competency-question research flagged the emitted deliverable and `Recurso` as separate unnamed gaps, and taking those names now would claim ground that belongs to them.

Indice.description: A bundle-scope index, regenerated from frontmatter
Indice.note: The 12th type, and the one addition to v1's catalog of 11. It exists because OKF requires typed frontmatter on every non-reserved .md, and `index.md`/`log.md` are the only reserved names -- so a bundle-level derived index such as PREGUNTAS-ABIERTAS.md needs a type to be conformant. Never hand-written: `brain derive` and `brain generate` own it.

reserved_files.note: The filenames OKF reserves, plus one of ours. `format` selects which structural check applies, so neither the name nor the rule is repeated in code.

index.md.note: directory index; no frontmatter except at the bundle root, which may carry okf_version only

log.md.note: date-grouped change history, newest first; headings are ISO YYYY-MM-DD

line_format.note: The line is an INTERFACE, not prose: `brain project` parses it into a `consultas` table so CQ-45 and CQ-46 can carry a `sql:` key like every other competency question. An interface with no spec and no check is the exact failure mode this repo exists to remove, so the shape is declared here and V26 enforces it. Anchored at end of line and parsed right-to-left, so the question text may contain anything -- including the separators. ONLY THE COUNTS ARE PROJECTED, never the question text: the two CQs need the numbers, and the text may carry what PERFIL.md marks confidential.
line_format.ejemplo_es: - ¿Qué decidimos sobre el bus de integración? — 12 docs (5 completos, 2 citados) · acotada · archivada
agent_rules_es: Una línea por consulta, bajo su `## AAAA-MM-DD`, lo más reciente arriba.
`docs` es cuántos documentos miraste en total; `completos` cuántos abriste enteros; `citados` cuántos de esos completos acabaron sosteniendo una afirmación de la respuesta.
`citados` nunca puede superar a `completos`: citar lo que no se abrió es lo que ADV-13 prohíbe.
`modo` es el de la compuerta de intención: `directa` si no abriste nada, `acotada` si el enunciado nombraba tipo, proyecto o persona, `abierta` si hubo que buscar.
Si la pregunta lleva un dato que PERFIL.md marca confidencial, registra el asunto y no el dato.
No escribas la razón citados/completos: se calcula al consultar. Un derivado dentro de un log es lo que este sistema no hace.

log-consultas.md.note: OURS, not OKF: what was ASKED of this brain, one line per query, written by /x-consultar. `log.md` records writes -- v1 had no record of a question, which is why the 9 `frequency` marks on the competency questions could not be closed by looking backwards (see the header of kernel/tests/competency-questions.yml) and why the 8.7x A/B verdict has an unmeasured half: A is measured per ingest, B per query. Kept OUT of log.md deliberately: that file is read by other skills to answer `what happened`, and reads are not changes. Same `log` format, so V3 already validates it and no code knew about it.

exempt_files.note: Exempt from the PROFILE checks only -- never from OKF conformance. OKF requires typed frontmatter on every non-reserved .md, so these still need a `type`; what they do not need is to match a catalog type's field set.
exempt_files.PERFIL.md: owner context in free prose; written by /x-setup

derived_files.note: Regenerated deterministically by `brain derive`. These grow with the brain; having the model rewrite them by hand is Slope A, the cost this contract exists to remove. Each entry declares what to select, how to filter, sort and render, so the engine knows nothing about this brain's types by name. Each also declares the `type` its generated frontmatter carries, so a derived file is fully OKF-conformant with nobody maintaining it.

02-areas/personas/ORGANIGRAMA.md.note: v1 shipped this as type Diagrama with no proyecto, clase or version. Generating it supplies all three, so the defect becomes impossible rather than merely detectable. A missing reporta-a is a declared gap, rendered as such -- never inferred.

projection.note: Cut-2 SQLite projection. Declared here rather than in the generator for the same reason as everything else in this file: `kernel/schema/ddl.sql` is a GENERATED artifact and V14 watches it, so whatever decides its content must be contract -- otherwise the DDL would have two sources of truth and the guard would only watch one. The acceptance criterion of T4 says it outright: adding a field, or a whole data type, must change the DDL WITHOUT touching code. The projection itself is derived and disposable: never versioned, rebuilt from the markdown, which stays the source of truth.
projection.engine_note: Measured on the target machine: SQLite 3.50.4, the 8 capabilities the competency questions need, whole corpus projected in 32 ms. DuckDB was dropped -- its columnar advantage does not show at this size and its cost (a wheel to install where pip is restricted) does. `sqlite3` is stdlib, so the zero-dependency invariant reaches cut 2 intact.

database.note: Relative to the working directory, not to the bundle: the projection is derived and disposable, and `.gitignore` already keeps `_db/` out. R9 allows it beside the bundle -- what it must never be is inside a synced folder, which `sqlite-probe.py` checks by attempting WAL.

projection.identifier_rule: Table and column identifiers are the type or field name, lowercased, with `-` replaced by `_`, and always double-quoted in the DDL. `fecha-creacion` becomes `fecha_creacion`. Quoting everything costs nothing and removes the whole class of reserved-word collisions.
projection.null_rule: A column is NOT NULL when its field is required AND its severity is not relaxed. A requirement carrying `severity: warning` is one the corpus is still migrating towards -- projecting it as NOT NULL would make the projector refuse documents that the validator merely warns about, which is a stricter rule than the contract's own. A `map` flattened into columns inherits its parent's requirement: `generated` is required but relaxed, so `generated_by` and `generated_at` are nullable -- otherwise the projector would refuse a document the contract accepts.

synthetic_columns.note: Columns the projector knows and that no document declares. They are deliberately NOT `common_fields`: that block is the contract of what someone WRITES, and a `path` written inside a document is a derived value stored by hand -- move the file and the field lies. A `hash` inside the content is worse, because writing it changes what it hashes. (`resumen_hash` of T2 is the legitimate case of the same shape: it hashes the BODY, not itself.)

path.from: bundle-relative path of the file -- the identity of the row

hash.from: SHA-256 of the file; T5 reprojects only what changed

synthetic_columns.note_projected_at: A `projected_at` column was declared in T4 and REMOVED in T5, before it ever shipped. It made two projections of identical content differ, which quietly breaks the acceptance criterion of T5 -- `--full` must be indistinguishable from an incremental pass. And it was redundant: what anyone actually asks is whether a row is up to date, and `hash` answers exactly that. A column that costs a real property and duplicates another one is not worth its bytes.

timeline.note: The event view of T6 is built from EVERY field with `data_type: date`, by rule and never by listing names -- listing them by hand is how the first version silently dropped `Pregunta.fecha-creacion` and `Plan.ultima-revision`. A field that is a date but not an event opts out with `timeline: false` and says why in its own `note`. Decided 2026-09-13, when counting against the generated DDL showed six date fields where the plan claimed five.
timeline.rule: every field with data_type `date`, unless it declares `timeline: false`
timeline.view_note: One row per dated field, not per document: a type with two date fields produces two events, which is why the view carries `campo`. Its shape -- fecha, tipo, campo, doc, title, and the scope field -- is structure rather than configuration, so it lives in the generator; what is declared here is what can change without changing code: the name, the direction, and which field scopes a query to one initiative. `order: desc` matches `log.md`, where the most recent is on top: someone reconstructing what happened reads backwards from now.

scope_view.note: `proyecto` is declared by nine types, so «everything about project X» would otherwise be a nine-way UNION retyped inside every query that needs it -- and stale the day a tenth type gets the field. Generated from whoever declares the scope field, like the timeline and the validity views.

query_log.note: `log-consultas.md` projected as one more table, so CQ-45 and CQ-46 carry a `sql:` like every other question instead of being exempted for living in markdown. The shape comes from `reserved_files["log-consultas.md"].line_format`, which V26 already enforces -- the projector parses what the validator checks, so there is no second reading of the same line. ONLY THE COUNTS: the question text may carry what PERFIL.md marks confidential, and the two CQs need numbers, not words.

search.note: FTS5 full-text index, populated in the same pass as the projection. It returns PATHS AND RANK, never content: handing back snippets would put the reader back where cut 2 started, reading text to decide what to read. What makes finding cheap is choosing well with L0/L1 and then opening few. The permission to skip dense vectors is empirical, not a concession: the ablation in the Agent Zero paper (table 7) measures our exact restriction -- lexical-only loses 1.8 points against hybrid, grep-only 1.6, and all three restricted variants still beat the best external system.
search.tokenize_note: Spanish is the default language of a brain: without `remove_diacritics`, `migracion` would not find `migración` and the index would be a trap for whoever types without accents. Value 2 also folds the diacritics that carry meaning in other languages, which is the right trade here and would not be in, say, a French corpus.
search.degrade_note: FTS5 is a compile flag, not a version: a perfectly recent SQLite can lack it. When it is missing the projection still runs WITHOUT the index and says so, naming `sqlite-probe.py` -- losing search is worse than losing nothing, but losing the whole projection because search is unavailable is worse still.

child_tables.note: D3, option A: structured fields are normalised -- never a comma-joined string, never a JSON blob. `json1` is compiled in, but STRICT is what makes the engine reject the wrong type, and `sources`/`verified` are precisely the governance fields the competency questions ask about. Three rules and no per-name exceptions, so a new structured field grows its table without code.

rules.list_of_map: child table (doc, idx, one column per member of `fields`)
rules.map: inline columns on the parent table, named `{field}_{member}`

bundle_schema.note: The single generated human-readable spec. A separate kernel-side CATALOGO.md existed and was deleted: it carried the same tables, and its only real advantage -- richer columns -- was an accident of improving one file and not the other. One derived spec, living where the documents are. Content of the portable ESQUEMA.md written into the bundle. It lives here rather than in code because it is content, not configuration: it is what someone who receives the `cerebro/` folder reads to understand it without the kernel. Spanish, like the rest of the bundle.
bundle_schema.resumen: Catálogo generado de los tipos de documento de este cerebro, con sus campos, sus valores admitidos, las convenciones de lectura y la clasificación de datos. Es lo que hace la carpeta autodescriptiva: quien la reciba puede entenderla sin el sistema que la produjo.
bundle_schema.title: Esquema de datos de este cerebro
bundle_schema.description: Cómo leer esta base de conocimiento: tipos, campos, convenciones y clasificación.
bundle_schema.intro: Este archivo hace al cerebro **autodescriptivo y portable**: cualquier persona o sistema que reciba la carpeta `cerebro/` puede entender su base de conocimiento leyendo esto, sin necesitar el kernel. Se genera desde el contrato; no se edita a mano.
conventions: **Bundle**: esta carpeta es la raíz. Los enlaces que empiezan con `/` se resuelven desde aquí.

**Puntero externo `/raw/...`**: apunta a las fuentes crudas del sistema que hospeda este cerebro, fuera del bundle. Si recibiste el cerebro sin sus fuentes, esos enlaces estarán rotos: es esperado, el conocimiento integrado está completo igual.
**Enlaces rotos**: se toleran. Representan conocimiento aún no escrito, no errores.

Todo `.md` de conocimiento lleva frontmatter con `type`. Se exceptúan `index.md` (índice por carpeta), `log.md` (historia de cambios, más reciente primero) y `log-consultas.md` (qué se le preguntó a este cerebro, una línea por consulta).
Las fuentes de cada afirmación van al final de cada documento, bajo `# Citations`.

structure.01-proyectos/: Trabajo con fecha de fin: una carpeta por proyecto, con su CONTEXT.md, insumos, reuniones, decisiones y preguntas.
structure.02-areas/: Responsabilidades continuas. Incluye `personas/` con las fichas y el organigrama, y lo que no es de ningún proyecto: `reuniones/`, `decisiones/` y `preguntas/`.
structure.03-recursos/: Referencia: sistemas y herramientas, glosario, los insumos y diagramas que no son de ningún proyecto, y lo que el rol necesite.

bundle_schema.classification_intro: Cada documento lleva un nivel de clasificación. Cada tipo tiene un **mínimo**: por debajo de él, el documento es inválido. Revisa esto antes de compartir o exportar el cerebro.
bundle_schema.types_intro: Los campos de cada tipo, con su obligatoriedad y valores admitidos. Suficiente para leer los datos —o regenerar las plantillas— sin el kernel.
bundle_schema.type_labels_note: Bundle-facing one-liner per type. The `description` on each type is engineering metadata in English, for the catalog and the JSON Schemas; this is the same thing said to the person who receives the brain, in the language of the brain. The renderer falls back to `description` when a label is missing.
